slides.title: Migration is 70% complete and on the original schedule
bullets: The remaining 6 services carry 80% of traffic
slides.visual: progress bar with all 20 services marked, the last 6 in a contrasting colour
slides.speaker_notes: We are at 70% with no customer impact. The remaining six services carry most of our traffic, so the last third is where the risk lives.

slides.title: Cut-over time fell by three quarters
bullets: Runbook rewrite took the median cut-over from 6 hours to 90 minutes
Rollback exercised twice in production, both clean
slides.speaker_notes: The runbook change is the reason we caught up. Rollback has been tested for real, not on paper.

slides.title: Availability held while latency improved
bullets: p95 latency down 12% after the second cut-over
slides.speaker_notes: Latency improved as a side effect of the new routing layer. Error budget is comfortable.

slides.title: Two issues are open and both have owners
bullets: On-call load is up 30% during cut-over weekends
slides.speaker_notes: Neither issue threatens the schedule yet. The billing dependency is the one to watch.

slides.title: The billing dependency is the schedule risk
bullets: Billing ships on 15 October, three weeks before the cut-over window
Fallback costs two extra weeks of dual-write
slides.speaker_notes: If billing slips past 15 October, we choose between missing the quarter or paying for the dual-write path.

slides.title: Two decisions are needed today
bullets: Accept the 15 October dependency as the plan of record
slides.visual: two decision cards with the owner of each
slides.speaker_notes: These are the only two things I need from this room.
